errors.current: After a verb or a preposition the ending is ـَيْنِ: أُرِيدُ كُوبَيْنِ.
errors.problem: Round-1 error #4 (the -īna/-ayni rule) was fixed in day 17 and in the day-20 objectives, but the day-20 intro still teaches 'after a verb … the ending is -ayni'. A dual that follows the verb as its SUBJECT keeps -āni (the same day's reading has يَأْكُلَانِ, and VSO sentences like يَأْكُلُ الْوَلَدَانِ are normal). Only the object of a verb, or a noun after a preposition, takes -ayni. A learner following the rule as written would produce *يَعْمَلُ الْمُوَظَّفَيْنِ.
errors.fix: As the object of a verb or after a preposition the ending is ـَيْنِ: أُرِيدُ كُوبَيْنِ.

Both are outside this chunk, but they are the same wrong rule.

errors.problem: In these intros the text presents تَ, يَ, نَ, يَـ as the person prefixes of the present tense ('تَ for you', 'يَ for he', 'with نَحْنُ the prefix is نَ', 'The prefix يَـ means he'). The tap names them only as letters, while أَ in the same intro gets 'a- (prefix of the present tense: I)'. A beginner who taps the prefix gets no meaning and an inconsistent message. These are not letter lists, so the 'bare letter = letter name' rule should not apply.
errors.fix: تَ=ta- (prefix of the present tense: you (m); she)
errors.alsoChange: يَ / يَـ=ya- (prefix of the present tense: he); نَ=na- (prefix of the present tense: we). Give vocalised single-letter prefixes with a haraka their own hand-glossary entries, like أَ.

errors.problem: مَحْشِي is written without the shadda on the yāʾ (the colloquial spelling). The MSA passive participle is مَحْشِيّ, and the very next line writes it correctly: الْمَحْشِيَّ. So the same word appears in two forms one line apart.

errors.path: dialogue.lines[2].ar (⟶ Wamādhā); dialogue.lines[9].ar (⟶ Wamatā, Wakayfa); dialogue.lines[11].ar (⟶ wahiya); content/days/day12.json sentences[5].ar (⟶ wayadrusu); content/days/day13.json dialogue.lines[6].ar (⟶ bisurʿa, walā); content/days/day14.json dialogue.lines[11].ar (⟶ bihādhā); content/days/day15.json dialogue.lines[3].ar (⟶ liʾannī); content/days/day17.json dialogue.lines[0].ar (⟶ liʾarbaʿa); content/days/day20.json dialogue.lines[7].ar (⟶ Wahal)
errors.problem: The Arabic is correct. The engine hyphenates a one-letter proclitic (وَ، بِ، لِ، فَ) only before hamza/al- or a name (wa-anā, bi-l-ḥāfila, wa-Laylā). Before any other consonant it fuses it into the word: Wamādhā, wahiya, wayadrusu, bisurʿa, bihādhā, falā, faṣadīquka. It also writes an internal ʾ instead of a hyphen: liʾannī, liʾarbaʿa. ALA-LC, the house style, is wa-mādhā, wa-hiya, bi-surʿa, li-anna, li-arbaʿa. In the romanised view the learner cannot see that وَ 'and' is a separate word, and the same clitic looks different from one line to the next. Round 1 listed this only as a note, but it is a systematic departure from the house style.
errors.fix: Engine: always output proclitic + hyphen (wa-mādhā, wa-hiya, bi-surʿa, li-annī, li-arbaʿa, fa-lā), capitalising only the first letter at the start of a sentence (Wa-mādhā).

summary: Read all 2,866 lines of days 11-20. I checked every Arabic string (sentences, mistake pairs, dialogues, readings, titles, culture notes, quiz prompts, options and answer keys) for harakat, case endings (object -an, idafa, after prepositions), present-tense conjugation (a-/ta-/ya-/na-, -īna, -ūna, dual -āni), the feminine-singular agreement of plurals of things, number-noun gender polarity (عَشْر كَلِمَات, لِأَرْبَعَة أَشْخَاص, سَبْعَةَ صُحُون, سَبْعَ مَلَاعِق, عَشَرَة أَرْغِفَة, ثَلَاثَة أَكْوَاب: all correct) and colour agreement. I also checked the translations and literals, all 1,721 seg glosses and all 643 tap glosses. All 70 quiz answer keys and every mistakes right/wrong pair are correct. The round-1 fixes are in place: الشَّاي → shāy, wa-Laylā/li-Sāmī, مَقْهًى, حَارّ = hot, spicy in day 18, the bare ة → tāʾ marbūṭa, and the day-17 -īna note. But the 'after a verb' rule survives in two places a learner sees: the day-20 intro, still major, and the طَبَّاخِينَ tap gloss on the day-17 quiz answer, also major. A softened version remains in the day-20 mistake note (minor). Errors: 6 (2 major, 4 minor). Tap glosses checked: 643. Wrong: 5. These are the طَبَّاخِينَ 'after a preposition or verb' gloss, plus 4 present-tense prefixes (تَ, يَ, نَ, يَـ) glossed only as letter names in intros that teach them as prefixes. The other errors are one spelling inconsistency (مَحْشِي vs الْمَحْشِيَّ) and one systematic engine issue: proclitics are fused instead of hyphenated (Wamādhā, wahiya, liʾarbaʿa). The Arabic of the chunk is otherwise clean.
